extracted.intended_audience: content marketers, PR professionals, and creators who want their content to attract news attention
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for content creators and PR practitioners on the journalistic news values that make content likely to be picked up or treated as newsworthy. Adapts classic journalism criteria to content marketing and publicity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: How a story affects readers' lives; the greater the number of people affected, the greater the impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the content meaningfully changes readers' circumstances, risks, benefits, or decisions. Example given: New fire engines reduce fire damage risk for community members (high impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers why information matters now; requires new information, discovery, or analysis — not necessarily a brand-new event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the story to a recent development, fresh data, or a new angle on existing facts to justify immediate attention. Examples: a newly-discovered dinosaur species or fresh analysis of old research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Why the source telling the story carries credibility; related to authority and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-known or authoritative sources to increase newsworthiness. Prominence can be conferred by the person or organization involved. Example: announcements by a state representative naturally merit coverage because of their position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the story matters to your specific audience — geographically or demographically relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize or target stories to the audience's location, community, or demographic interests to boost relevance and pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Bizarre
rubrics_metrics.description: Unexpected or unusual elements that break the norm and attract attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight surprising, counterintuitive, or novel details. The post invokes the classic line: 'When a dog bites a man, that's not news... if a man bites a dog, then that's news.' Use unusual hooks to stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple perspectives on an issue fighting for attention; tension or disagreement that generates emotional engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories around opposing viewpoints, debates, or controversies to create drama and reader interest. Note: political coverage often leverages disagreement rather than consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the idea trending or seasonally relevant? An idea whose time has come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect content to current trends, memes, seasonal moments, or viral phenomena to ride existing interest. Examples: the Ice Bucket Challenge or Valentine's Day–related stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories featuring people impacted by larger events that personalize broader narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on individual experiences, anecdotes, or profiles that put a human face on abstract topics to increase empathy and engagement.
